hook_text: Minus forty degrees in winter, snow for half the year, and a forest that stretches right around the top of the world. Where is it?
clip_script: A pine plantation near Sabie, rows of tall, dark trees with cones and needles. Their wild relatives grow in a huge belt across Canada, Scandinavia and Russia. Winters there are long and freezing, with snow for months. Summers are short and cool. The trees keep their needles all year, and their cone shape lets snow slide off. It is the largest forest on land, and it is all in the Northern Hemisphere.
visual_style: Whiteboard globe tilted to show a dark green belt across the top of North America, Europe and Asia, then a climate graph with a tall hill-shaped temperature line, then a snowy conifer shedding snow.
mood: Cool and calm, like a quiet walk in the snow.
pacing: A gentle start among the pines, then a clear map tour and a step-by-step climate graph.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and compare a coniferous forest climate graph with a rainforest graph.
